## How to Run a LinkedIn Outreach Campaign for Pre-Seed Investors in AI SaaS Startups (2026)


**Quick Answer:**[Origami](https://origami.chat/) has a built-in LinkedIn sequencer, so you can find pre-seed investors, enrich their contact data, and run the entire LinkedIn outreach campaign from one platform. You build the list, refine it, write or auto-generate a three-touch sequence, launch sends with configurable delays, and track replies without exporting a CSV.


This is the 2026 playbook for turning a target list into actual investor conversations. If you followed the parent post on[how to build a list of Pre-Seed Investors for AI SaaS Startups](https://origami.chat/blog/pre-seed-investors-ai-saas-startups) , you already have a list sitting in[Origami](https://origami.chat/) . This guide covers what to do next: how to refine that list for LinkedIn, what to say in each of three touches, and how to send it all natively from[Origami](https://origami.chat/) without switching tools.


Pre-seed investors see a dozen AI pitches every week. Most founders write generic notes and get ignored. The sequence below works because it treats investors like sharp, time-constrained buyers who need evidence, not enthusiasm.


## Step 1 — Build the List in[Origami](https://origami.chat/)


If you already have a list, skip to Step 2. If you need to rebuild or expand it, this is the exact prompt to type into[Origami](https://origami.chat/) :


> I'm looking for pre-seed investors actively investing in AI SaaS startups. Include angel investors, micro-VCs, scouts, and solo GPs. They should write checks between $100k and $1M, focus on B2B software, applied AI, or developer tools, and have a track record in the last two years. Exclude later-stage VCs, service providers, and dormant profiles. Output decision-makers with LinkedIn profiles, emails, and recent investment context.


[Origami](https://origami.chat/) returns a targeted list with verified names, titles, company details, LinkedIn profiles, emails, and phone numbers. You also get context on recent investments, thesis areas, and sometimes the tools an investor uses. That context is what makes the outreach feel specific instead of copied.


The free plan gives you 1,000 credits with no credit card. That is usually enough to test a small list and see the data quality before paying for more enrichment.


## Step 2 — Refine and Qualify the List


A raw list is not an outreach list. Pre-seed investors vary wildly in relevance, and sending to the wrong people wastes sequence slots.


Start by viewing the list in[Origami](https://origami.chat/) . Sort by company size, title, and location. Remove anyone whose title does not indicate investing: advisors, consultants, growth marketers, and startup operators are not pre-seed capital sources. Also remove investors whose last check was before 2023 or whose portfolio is all later-stage. For AI SaaS, you want investors who already understand software gross margins and AI model risk.


What a qualified pre-seed AI SaaS investor looks like:


- They have led or participated in at least one pre-seed or angel round in AI, B2B SaaS, developer tools, or applied AI in the last 18 months.
- Their typical check size matches your raise. If you are raising $500k to $1.5M, ignore funds with a $5M minimum.
- They are active on LinkedIn. This is the channel, so dormant profiles waste sequence slots.
- They are not service providers, consultants, or content creators posing as investors.
- They have a public thesis or portfolio that lets you reference a specific investment in the first touch.


Segment the list inside[Origami](https://origami.chat/) into buckets:


- Solo angels and syndicate leads (company size 1-5). They invest in 5-20 companies per year and respond to founder edge and early traction.
- Micro-fund partners (company size 2-20). They manage a small fund, need to show diligence to LPs, and respond to market size, differentiation, and a path to seed.
- Scouts or venture partners at larger funds who still write pre-seed checks. They respond to speed, hot deal signals, and warm intros.
- Geography. Focus on investors in your time zone first. Remote-first AI SaaS investors often sit in the US, UK, EU, or Singapore.


Why segment? A solo angel responds to traction and personal relationship. A micro-fund partner responds to market sizing and thesis fit. A scout responds to deal flow and speed. Segmenting lets you tweak the same sequence without rewriting everything.


Qualified means you would be comfortable mentioning a specific investment in the first LinkedIn note. If you cannot find a portfolio company to reference for an investor, they are either too dormant or too early for outreach.


## Step 3 — Create the LinkedIn Sequence


Here is the important part.[Origami](https://origami.chat/) has a built-in LinkedIn sequencer on all paid plans. You have two ways to create your sequence.


Option one: paste your own templates. Write a three-touch sequence, paste the templates into[Origami](https://origami.chat/) 's sequencer, set the delays between touches, and hit Launch. You control the copy and cadence.


Option two: let the agent write it. Ask[Origami](https://origami.chat/) 's AI agent to generate a personalized three-day LinkedIn sequence for all your leads automatically. The agent writes messages based on each lead's profile data — title, company, industry, and recent activity — so every message feels custom instead of copied.


Before you paste any template, make sure your variables are specific. A bad placeholder like \[value prop\] kills the sequence. A good placeholder is \[Company A\] or \[their focus\]. The agent can also pull those fields from enriched data if you ask it to generate the sequence.


Below is a full three-touch sequence I have used for pre-seed AI SaaS investor outreach. Each message is 50-100 words, direct, and specific to this audience. Replace bracketed placeholders with your details. Do not send this without personalization.


Day 1 — Connection request + note


Subject line: N/A for connection request. LinkedIn uses the note as the only text.


Hi \[First Name\], I'm building \[Startup\], an AI-native \[category\] that helps \[target customer\] do \[specific outcome\] without \[pain point\]. I saw you backed \[Company A\] and \[Company B\] at pre-seed, and I think our approach to \[technical moat\] is in the same lane. Would be great to connect as I share early traction and product updates. No pitch — just building in public.


Why it works: it proves you did your homework on their portfolio, names two specific bets, and makes a low-pressure ask.


Day 3 — Follow-up message


Subject line: quick follow-up on \[Startup\]


Hi \[First Name\], I know pre-seed AI is noisy right now, so I'll keep this brief. Since my connection request, we have \[milestone — for example, signed 3 design partners or shipped our first agent\]. Given your thesis in \[their focus\], one thing might interest you: our users are showing \[specific insight\], which suggests \[market shift\]. If useful, I can share a 15-minute demo with the numbers. If not, no worries — happy to stay connected.


Why it works: it respects the investor's time, references a milestone that came after the connection request, and offers a concrete next step without a hard pitch.


Day 7 — Final message


Subject line: closing the loop


Hi \[First Name\], I'll assume timing isn't right for a deeper look. If you're open to it, I'd still like to send you our monthly builder update — one email, no pitch. It covers what we're shipping, metrics we're watching, and one hard lesson from building in AI SaaS. Otherwise, I'll leave it here. Thanks for the connection, and good luck with \[recent fund activity or portfolio company\].


Why it works: it closes the loop gracefully, removes pressure, and leaves a low-lift way to stay in touch. Investors remember founders who don't spam.


One more note on subject lines: LinkedIn shows the first line of the message as the preview. Keep that first line short and specific, because it decides whether the investor opens the full message.


Customizing by segment:


- For solo angels, change the Day 3 milestone to something about founder speed or customer love. They care about momentum.
- For micro-fund partners, change the Day 3 angle to market size or a specific enterprise use case. They need to justify diligence to LPs.
- For scouts, change Day 7 to offer a quick deal memo. They move fast and hate long follow-up chains.


## Step 4 — Send the Sequence Directly from[Origami](https://origami.chat/)


You do not need to export the list, sync it to another tool, or import CSVs. You launch the sequence directly from[Origami](https://origami.chat/) .


For the sending step, review[Origami’s email and LinkedIn sequencer](https://origami.chat/products/sequencer) before setting up your campaign.


The built-in LinkedIn sequencer sends connection requests and follow-up messages automatically with configurable delays between touches. Set the cadence in the sequencer. The example above uses Day 1, Day 3, and Day 7, but you can adjust it.


Once a sequence is running, you see opens, clicks, and replies in the same dashboard where you built the list. There is no second tool to check. While viewing a contact's activity, you can still see their enriched profile — title, company, tools used, and investment focus. That context reminds you why you reached out in the first place.


If someone replies, they automatically unenroll from the rest of the sequence. That prevents the classic mistake of sending a follow-up or breakup message after a meeting is already booked.


This is the biggest shift in how[Origami](https://origami.chat/) works now: it is not just a list-building tool. It handles the full workflow — find, enrich, sequence, send, and track. The LinkedIn sequencer is included on all paid plans. You only pay for credits used to enrich leads. The sending itself is free on paid plans.


What response rate should you expect for pre-seed AI SaaS investors? With a tightly qualified list, I typically see 25-40% connection acceptance and 5-12% positive replies. Meeting bookings from cold LinkedIn are usually lower, around 1-5%, but that can compound when you combine LinkedIn with follow-up email or warm referrals. If your acceptance rate is below 20%, the problem is usually the list, not the message. Tighten the qualification, remove dormant profiles, or segment further. If acceptance is solid but replies are weak, iterate on the second message. Try a different angle, shorten the ask, or test a subject line that references a specific portfolio company.


When someone replies, move fast. If the reply is positive, ask for a 15-minute call or offer two specific times. If the reply is not interested, send one polite line: Thanks for letting me know. I'll send the monthly update unless you tell me not to. Then unenroll manually if[Origami](https://origami.chat/) has not already done it.
